title: Ordinary tensor comparison and flat representatives on a ringed site
statement: For essentially small sites C,D with independent coefficient universe containing both site universes, let U:C→D be continuous and representably flat. Let R,S be commutative ring sheaves and a:R→U_*S a structural ring map. For any specified additive left adjoint F⊣a_*, F preserves K-flat complexes having flat terms. There is a unique family of ordinary tensor isomorphisms F(M⊗N)≅FM⊗FN, natural in M,N and sending each restricted scalar multiple of the adjunction-unit image of a pure tensor to the tensor of the two corresponding unit generators. No derived category or total chain comparison is asserted. [def-coef-semilinear-system-models] Equivalently this is unique ordinary comparison data [def-sf-ordinary-tensor-pullback-data], whose remaining fields are propositions.

proof.text: Construct geometric inverse image using representable flatness; transfer ring and module operations and extend scalars along the adjunct of a. The two tensor maps send (x⊗y)⊗r to (x⊗r)⊗(y⊗1) and (x⊗r)⊗(y⊗s) to (x⊗y)⊗rs. Balancing, commutativity and sheafification show that they are inverse. Uniqueness of left adjoints transports this construction to the specified adjunction, preserving its unit. Keep the scalar-extension functor abstract through its exact object and morphism presentation when transporting its tensor and flatness properties. Retain the concrete geometric lift through its ring and module presentation before forming the structural ring map.

Evaluate the set-sheaf adjunction unit on a pure tensor. Naturality with the pure pairing and both projections gives the ordinary module unit formula after cancelling the transported comparison. Restrict this equality to every site arrow and multiply by a local scalar. The module adjunction and pure-tensor generation prove uniqueness; naturality transports along the same comparison. Pure-section extensionality is the generic sheafification lemma in the tensorator construction, so the coefficient-specialized ordinary reduction is not needed. Evaluate the inverse-image pairing and scalar linearity first as section lemmas with abstract modules; reuse them after pullback specialization.
Apply ringed-topos pullback preservation of K-flat complexes with flat terms, then transport across the same left-adjoint isomorphism.

theorem sitePullbackTensorGenerators
    {C D : Type c} [Category.{v} C] [Category.{v} D]
    [EssentiallySmall.{r} C] [EssentiallySmall.{r} D]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    (U : C ⥤ D) [U.IsContinuous J K] [RepresentablyFlat U]
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{r}) (S : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{r})
    (φ : R ⟶ (U.sheafPushforwardContinuous CommRingCat.{r} J K).obj S)
    (F : SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, r} J R ⥤
      SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, r} K S) [F.Additive]
    (adj : F ⊣ SheafOfModules.pushforward.{r}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).map φ)) :
    ∃! _data : OrdinaryTensorPullbackData.{c, v, r} J K U R S φ F adj, True
